subject: Production: LuminaPay inference latency spike & 503s — urgent
messages:
From: Daniel Ortega <daniel.ortega@luminapay.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T08:15:00Z
Subject: High latency + 503s on production since 06:00 UTC

Hi Soojin —

We started seeing a large increase in end-to-end latency and intermittent 503s hitting our inference endpoints around 06:00 UTC. Throughput dropped ~40% and some of our payment-critical flows are timing out. We believe we have reserved capacity, so this is surprising.

Attached: a short sample of error logs and a dashboard screenshot. Can you triage immediately? Our ops pager is also firing. We are on a partial freeze and need an ETA.

—Daniel Ortega
Head of Platform, LuminaPay
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T08:28:00Z
Subject: URGENT: LuminaPay PROD degradation — need triage + exec flag

Team —

Customer LuminaPay is reporting elevated latency and 503s in production; they claim reserved capacity should prevent this. Details below from the customer and attached logs (see attachments).

Impact: payment pipelines degraded (~40% throughput drop) — customer requests immediate mitigation and an ETA. They are on a bridge (link in related_links).

Ask:
- Marcus / Dev: can you immediately validate whether LuminaPay's reserved pool is being saturated or if noisy co-tenants are impacting shared nodes? Check GPU util, queue lengths, and autoscaler events for the last 4 hours.
- Marissa: own customer comms and coordinate the bridge (they need continuous updates).
- Rishi: FYI — this may need an executive touch if we cannot provide a fast remediation or if credits are required.

Next steps: please post findings in this thread within 20 minutes. If mitigation requires capacity bump, propose the minimal change we can do without violating other reserved commitments.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: LuminaPay PROD degradation — need triage + exec flag

Quick initial triage (preliminary):
- Observed on the node group hosting LuminaPay's reserved pool: two nodes are at sustained 98-100% GPU utilization starting ~05:50 UTC.
- Autoscaler shows failed scale-up events: new nodes attempted but allocation timed out due to scheduling contention (driver init + kernel memory pressure).
- Concurrently, a large multi-tenant job (not in reserved pool) started around 05:40 and pinned memory on shared infra; it looks like the noisy workload bled into edge resource managers and prevented timely allocation of new capacity.

Attachments: short metrics screenshot (pool-metrics-20270403.png). I will pull deeper logs (nv-hostengine + scheduler) and post within 30m.

Immediate mitigation options (quick list):
1) Evacuate noisy tenant processes from nodes adjacent to LuminaPay's pool (fast, ~10-15m, but may impact other customers).
2) Route LuminaPay traffic to a cold spare pool we can warm (estimated 8-12m to warm model caches).
3) Temporary capacity bump (provision 2 GPUs into LuminaPay's reserved pool) — requires infra action and possible exec sign-off since it affects capacity accounting.

I recommend 2) + 3) in parallel: route traffic to the spare pool to stop the customer impact, then provision a temporary bump if that reduces latency and errors.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: LuminaPay PROD degradation — need triage + exec flag

On the customer bridge now. Confirming impact: multiple merchant flows are timing out, risk of failed payouts if this persists >30m. Customer requests that we either (a) route traffic to a fallback pool immediately or (b) guarantee performance with a 3-day goodwill credit if we cannot restore within 30 minutes.

Customer sentiment: escalated — they will request their legal/procurement to open a dispute if transaction failures are observed. They explicitly called out the reserved capacity guarantee.

I support Marcus's plan 2) as the fastest commutable mitigation. Please start the reroute and let me know exact ETA so I can update the customer. If we need to provision GPUs temporarily, we should also propose a credit (see attached proposed-credit-sheet.xlsx) as a customer retention measure.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T09:18:00Z
Subject: Exec decision needed: temporary capacity bump + customer credit for LuminaPay

Rishi —

Summary: Marcus confirmed noisy-tenant induced allocation failures led to LuminaPay reserved-pool throughput shortfall. Marissa reports high customer impact (payment timeouts). Proposed remediation: route to a warmed spare pool immediately; provision +2 GPUs into their reserved pool as a temporary bump (3-6 hours) to stabilize. Customer asks for 3-day goodwill credit if we cannot fully recover within 30m. They may escalate to procurement/legal.

Recommendation: approve the temporary capacity bump and pre-approve up to $X equivalent in credits (I drafted a number in the attached sheet; see proposed-credit-sheet.xlsx). Approving now allows infra to proceed without delaying mitigation.

If you prefer, we can commit to the reroute only and revisit credits after impact analysis, but the customer is already asking for an exec-level assurance.

Thanks —
Soojin
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Exec decision needed: temporary capacity bump + customer credit for LuminaPay

Approved: proceed with Marcus's recommended mitigation path.
- Marissa: inform the customer we are routing traffic to a warmed spare pool (ETA to customer: 10-15m).
- Dev/Marcus: provision +2 GPUs into LuminaPay's reserved entitlement for up to 6 hours; log the capacity delta and create an RU (resource usage) ticket.
- Finance/Sales: pre-approve a provisional credit equal to 3 days of committed usage (we will reconcile after incident report). Marissa, please note this is provisional pending final damage assessment.

Additionally: Marcus, capture timeline and root cause details; we will need a post-incident review and an action plan to avoid noisy-tenant bleed in reserved pools (policy/placement changes).

Thanks team — prioritize customer stability.

—Rishi
VP, Customer Operations
